changes.text: 另一种解释是关于措辞的分工：他把“革命”换成“改良”，把结论降格为“刍议”，自己承担温和的发表风险；陈独秀随后把它高举为“文学革命”，由更激进的人去举旗。据胡适转述，陈独秀坦白说首举义旗的是胡适，他自己高张大旗作声援。这种“一人放低、一人举高”的配合，是作者从先后次序读出的一种可能，属本文的推断。

A second reading concerns the division of labour over words. He swapped revolution for reform and demoted his conclusion to a humble opinion, taking on himself the risk of publishing moderately; Chen Duxiu then raised it as literary revolution, and a more radical man carried the flag. By Hu's report, Chen said frankly that the banner was Hu's and that he himself was raising it high in support. This doubling — one man lowering the volume, one raising it — is a possibility the author reads in the sequence; it is this article's inference.
本文只有胡适晚年口述一种来源，且经节译、手订与回译；梅光迪、任鸿隽的言行均为胡适转述，胡适对动机的说明是事后自述，唐德刚的注释属评论而非史实。凡标为 interpretation 的段落是作者推断，标为 modern 的段落是为今日读者虚构的场景。

This piece rests on a single source: Hu Shi's oral memoir in later life, itself abridged, revised in his own hand and translated back. Mei Guangdi's and Ren Hongjun's words and deeds reach us only through Hu's retelling; Hu's explanations of motive are retrospective; and Tang Degang's notes are commentary rather than fact. Paragraphs marked interpretation are the author's inferences, and paragraphs marked modern are scenarios invented for readers today.

Hu's own explanation of how it all happened is that he opposed single-cause theories of history. He used to joke that accidents often matter more than any monistic cause — economics, lust, God and the rest: those single causes explain everything that has ever happened, and precisely because they explain everything, they explain nothing. In this episode he explicitly called the farewell poem a small accident, and said that a chain of small accidents had gradually forced him into his position; placing the leaflet and the dispute that followed the near-capsize on the lake in that chain is this article's own grouping. Reading a chain of small accidents as the push behind his position is Hu's own view of history, not a finding of this article.

胡适自己对来龙去脉的解释是反对单因论。他开玩笑说，历史上的意外事件往往比“单因”——经济、色欲、上帝之类——更重要：正因为这些单因对所有事件皆可解释，它们也就不可解释任何事件。就他这段经历而言，他明确把送别诗称作「意外的小事」，并说「一连串的小意外事件，逐渐地强迫我采取了这个立场」；本文把传单和湖上险些翻船引出的争论也放进这一串，这是本文的归并。把一连串小意外看作推力，是他本人的史观，不是本文的结论。

After the note was sent, he regretted it. Zhong was a kind man with a sincere wish to reform Chinese customs and writing; the rudeness was uncalled for, and Hu reproached himself before his friends. Then a further thought: if men like Zhong are not qualified to discuss such questions, then the qualified should do the work — set out what is feasible and what is not, and examine both. He took it up with Zhao Yuanren, who had entered Cornell with him in 1910. They agreed to make the question of China's writing (in our translation) the literature section's topic for the annual meeting of the Chinese Students' Association in the East, and split it: Zhao on whether the Chinese script could adopt an alphabetic system and how to proceed; Hu on, in our translation, how to make our classical written language easier to teach.

字条寄出后他心中懊悔，觉得不该对一位和善又有心改革语言文字的人如此不礼貌，于是在朋友面前自我谴责，并想到一层：假如钟君这样的人不够资格谈这个问题，那么够资格的人实在更该认真研究，把可行与不可行的问题都摆出来检讨。他找上1910年同进康乃尔的赵元任，两人商定把“中国文字的问题”作为美东中国学生会文学股年会的论题，各写一篇：赵元任论吾国文字能否采用字母制及其进行方法，他论“如何可使吾国文言易于教授”。

Hu's paper called the classical written language — in our translation — a half-dead language. Some words live, some have died: gou, "dog," is still in use; quan, the old word for the same animal, is not. "Ride a horse" is everyday speech; the classical equivalent is a dead phrase. So the teaching of a living language and of a half-dead one must be very different business. Looking back, he said his doctrine — vernacular alive, classical half-dead — had begun in this period.
在那篇论文里，他提出文言是「半死的语言」。理由很具体：有些词还活着，有些已经死了——“狗”字今天仍在用，“犬”字就不用了；“骑马”仍是日常用语，“乘马”事实上已不通行。所以教活的语言和教半死的语言，方法应该大不相同。他晚年回忆说，自己后来“白话是活的语言、文言半死”的主张，就是从这个时期开始的。

It appeared in New Youth in January 1917 and stirred a great response. Two Peking University professors took it seriously. Chen Duxiu, an unbending revolutionary, answered with "On Literary Revolution," publicly backing a literary revolution and saying frankly that the banner had been raised by his friend Hu Shi; he himself was raising the banner high in his friend's support. Qian Xuantong, professor of classical phonology, a master of ancient prose and a disciple of the great scholar Zhang Taiyan, wrote no article but sent Chen and Hu long letters — small criticisms, great praise — also printed in New Youth; that so eminent a classicist should sympathize buoyed their cause. Zhao Yuanren often said, in our translation, that Hu's vernacular poems and essays were not vernacular enough, not the genuine spoken style ordinary people used. Hu admitted it: like a woman who had bound her feet for forty, or even twenty, years, however much she loosened the bindings she would never recover natural feet.

1917年一月，文章在《新青年》刊出，文化界反应很大。北大有两位教授重视它：一位是陈独秀本人，本是死硬派的革命人物，随后写《文学革命论》响应，公开支持文学革命，并说首举义旗的是朋友胡适，自己高张大旗作声援；另一位是古典音韵学教授、章太炎门人钱玄同，这位古文大家没有写文章，却写去小批评大捧场的长信，也在《新青年》发表，声势为之一振。赵元任则常说胡适的白话诗文“不够白”，不是一般人常用的真正语体；胡适承认了，打了个比方：像裹了四十年或者二十年小脚的女人，纵使把小脚放大，终究恢复不了天足。
